question: Is Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu safe for beginners?
summary: Yes. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu at Sensei Sandy BJJ is safe for beginners. Training begins with a studio tour, a safety walkthrough, and clear rules. Every drill is coach-led with carefully matched partners, controlled movement, and mutual tapping. You set your own pace from day one.
answer: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu is a grappling martial art based on leverage, balance, and body position rather than striking. At our Tannersville studio, class size is capped at 12 students so Coach Sandy can guide every partner interaction. Students learn how to fall safely, how to tap to signal a reset, and how to practice with care. Beginners start in our Beginner Lane, practicing cooperative movement at a calm, comfortable pace.

question: At what age can children start BJJ?
summary: Children can start Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu at age 5 at Sensei Sandy BJJ. Our Youth classes welcome kids ages 5 to 9, and our Teen classes serve youth ages 10 to 17. Younger children learn through active movement games that build balance, focus, and body control.
answer: For kids ages 5 to 9, classes focus on body awareness, coordination, following coach directions, and working respectfully with a partner. We teach children how to move safely, protect their heads, and solve physical problems using leverage. Parents are always welcome to stay and watch every youth class from matside.

question: Do I need to be physically fit before starting?
summary: You can start Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu at any fitness level. Training is how you build stamina, strength, and mobility. Classes begin with calm, coach-guided pacing, and Coach Sandy adjusts each activity to fit your current comfort.
answer: Adults of all backgrounds and body types train at Sensei Sandy BJJ. We prioritize leverage and technique over brute force. You can pause, rest, or adjust intensity during any drill. Simply wear comfortable athletic clothes and start at your own speed.

question: What should I expect during my first BJJ class?
summary: Your first visit begins with a 15-minute room tour and conversation with Coach Sandy. You see the clean mats, learn studio safety rules, and discuss your personal goals. For your first coached class, you are paired with a calm, experienced partner for gentle, step-by-step movement drills.
answer: You will experience pure encouragement and cooperative learning from day one. You wear comfortable athletic clothes. Coach Sandy introduces fundamental positions, safe movement, and how tapping allows partners to reset comfortably. You will always know what comes next, and you can ask questions at any point. Your first class is a free coached learning experience.

question: How often should beginners train?
summary: Beginners progress best by training 2 to 3 times per week. This rhythm gives your body adequate time to recover while reinforcing new movement patterns, muscle memory, and positional awareness each week.
answer: Consistency matters more than intensity. Attending two or three small-group classes each week allows techniques to feel natural and comfortable. Our schedule offers weekday youth classes at 5:00 PM, adult classes at 6:00 PM, and Saturday morning sessions, with open-seat rescheduling by text if family or work plans change.

question: Does Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu help build children's confidence?
summary: Yes. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu builds genuine confidence through earned accomplishment. By learning how to escape holds, protect their balance, and solve physical challenges against gentle resistance, children discover they can handle difficult situations with calm focus.
answer: Unlike activities based on rote memorization, Jiu-Jitsu gives children tangible feedback in real time. They see their progress as they learn to defend themselves, respect training partners, and speak up when they need help. Parents frequently report improvements in focus at school, better emotional control at home, and quiet self-assurance.

question: Where can I take Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu classes near Hunter or Tannersville?
summary: You can take Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu classes at Sensei Sandy BJJ, located at 6045 Main Street (2nd Floor Studio) in Tannersville, NY. The studio is just 4 miles from Hunter and easily accessible from Windham, Haines Falls, and Mountaintop communities across the Catskills.
answer: We are located right on Main Street in Tannersville, inside Studios on Main, with ample street parking nearby. We offer dedicated classes for Kids (ages 5–9), Teens (ages 10–17), and Adults (18+), as well as private morning coaching. Families and visitors traveling from Hunter, Windham, Phoenicia, and Catskill can book a Free First Visit to meet Coach Sandy and tour the academy.

question: What should I wear to my first class?
summary: Wear clean, comfortable athletic clothing, such as a t-shirt or rash guard and athletic shorts or sweatpants. Choose clothing free of zippers, snaps, buttons, or metal hardware to protect your partners and the mats.
answer: You train in bare feet on clean mats. We recommend bringing a water bottle and slip-on shoes or flip-flops to wear off the mat. We provide loaner gis and uniforms for subsequent classes.

question: Can parents watch youth classes?
summary: Yes. Parents and guardians are always welcome to watch small-group youth classes from comfortable matside seating. Staying to observe helps you see our positive coaching style and watch your child learn.
answer: We encourage parents to observe how Coach Sandy leads drills and pairs students. You can see how we handle pacing, safety, and encouragement first-hand, and speak with Sandy directly after class.

question: What does the first visit cost?
summary: Your first visit and introductory class are completely free. You can meet Coach Sandy, tour the facility, learn about our programs, and experience coached movement before deciding on any paid enrollment.
answer: There is no financial commitment required to try. After your free introductory session, Sandy will share program details and membership options so you can choose what best fits your family.

question: Can I reschedule if my plans change?
summary: Yes. We make rescheduling simple and personal. You can coordinate makeups or change your class times by sending a text directly to Sandy at +1 (917) 736-8649.
answer: We understand mountain weather, family events, and busy work schedules. Our open-seat text coordination helps you maintain training consistency with complete ease.

question: Do you teach MMA or Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu at Sensei Sandy?
summary: Sensei Sandy BJJ teaches Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu. BJJ is the foundational ground control and submission discipline used in modern MMA.
answer: Our Tannersville studio focuses purely on safe, cooperative grappling, positional balance, and gentle joint control. You learn practical self-defense and athletic conditioning in a friendly, respectful room.
